findings.detail: The question stem and the reason for option B call the automated actor 'the CI runner', but option A calls it 'the CI job'. One actor has two names.

blind_answer.reason: Splitting the 900-line file into topic files such as testing.md and api-conventions.md in the project's .claude/rules/ directory gives each topic its own maintainable file, which reduces merge conflicts. Because the rules live in the project and are version-controlled, every developer and the CI runner still receive them. B fails because user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md files are not shared with teammates or CI. A fails because slash commands load only when invoked, not automatically. D fails because it keeps the single monolithic file, so the merge conflicts remain.
